summary: Sustained 5xx surge for tenant after connection-throttle causing runtime page-faults and KV-cache fragmentation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusAI experiencing a sustained increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood API for requests routed to their dedicated pool in us-east. Error rate started ~2026-03-13T03:20Z and persisted with periodic spikes. Upstream logs show connection resets to the serving runtime and a correlated rise in runtime page-fault counters and KV-cache fragmentation metrics.

Impact:
- ~18% error rate (5xx) across tenant's traffic during surge windows.
- Several long streaming sessions cut with HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and 502 responses.
- Customer production features degraded; reporting user-facing errors.

Environment: prod|us-east, tenant: NimbusAI (dedicated), model pin: redwood-3b-v1 (fallback to open-llama-7b observed).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant issues a burst of ~3x normal concurrent streaming sessions and high fanout prefetched requests.
2) API gateway begins queueing and applying connection throttles to upstream proxies.
3) Upstream serving runtime shows increased page-fault rate and slower KV cache SSTable compaction/gc cycles.
4) Runtime starts returning connection resets and 502/503s to the gateway, amplifying client retries and further load.

Evidence / logs:
- API gateway logs (gw-us-east-02): repeated 502 with upstream reset: "upstream prematurely closed connection" at 2026-03-13T03:22:11Z.
- Runtime logs (runtime-tenant-045): high page-faults per sec metric from host-agent starting 03:21Z; OOM not observed.
- KV cache fragmentation gauge spiked from baseline 4% to 47% between 03:20Z-03:30Z.
- Traces: distributed traces show long tail in prefetch/key-lookup step and TCP retransmits.
- Customer report: "multiple users see temporary failures and some streaming sessions closed unexpectedly".

Hypothesis:
The tenant's burst pattern triggered API gateway connection throttling which created uneven request routing and head-of-line blocking on a subset of runtime workers. This, combined with a pathological prefetch pattern from the customer's workload, caused KV-cache to fragment and increased page-fault activity (cold pages + kernel memory churn). The runtime's kernel selection/fallback path kicked in (kernel swap) leading to slower token processing and upstream connection resets. Retry amplification then produced sustained elevated 5xx.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced a traffic pattern in staging with similar tenant pinning: observed the same KV fragmentation trend when prefetch_size > 8 and concurrent_streams > 120.
- Heap and GPU memory stable; page-faults tied to host kernel page-in activity, not GPU OOM.
- Autoscaler did not scale fast enough due to backlog visibility lag in the scheduler metrics.
- Routing logs show ~27% of tenant's requests were pinned to a small subset of runtime pods during the initial ramp.
- SRE sampling against runtime kernel config shows a compatibility fallback path used by the model runner on affected pods (kernel_fallback=true).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Applied an emergency soft-connection-limit for the tenant at the API gateway for 30 minutes to slow the burst and prevent retries from amplifying errors. (Actioned 2026-03-13T03:45Z)
- Manual rolling restart of the 4 affected runtime pods to clear kernel fallback state and reduce page-fault backlog. (Started 03:50Z, completed 04:04Z)
- Temporarily disabled aggressive prefetch for tenant at the routing layer (prefetch_size=2).

Current status:
- Error rate reduced to ~3% post-mitigations but periodic spikes observed when customer resumes heavy bursts.
- Customer notified and in coordination with CS to throttle their client-side prefetch while we implement longer-term controls.

Proposed long-term fixes / action items:
1) Runtime: add guardrails for kernel_fallback path to prefer graceful degradation over slow path activation for pinned tenants. (ENG-6401)
2) Autoscaler: improve backlog-aware scaling triggers so aggregate queue depth on a tenant triggers earlier scale-ups. (ENG-6322)
3) API gateway: implement tenant-specific burst circuit-breaker and adaptive retry pacing to prevent retry storms. (ENG-6390)
4) KV-cache: investigate compaction/gc tuning to better tolerate tenant prefetch patterns; add metrics for fragmentation heatmaps. (ENG-6360)
5) Postmortem and customer playbook: document recommended client-side limits for concurrent streams and prefetch sizes. (OPS-510)

Resolution notes (work-in-progress):
- Short-term workarounds (gateway soft-limits, reduced prefetch, rolling restarts) have restored service to an acceptable level for the customer.
- Engineering tickets created for the systemic items; timeline requested from ENG on 2026-03-15.

Attachments / links:
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenants/nimbusai/error-rate
- Trace sample: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/9f3c2a1b
- SRE runbook excerpt: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Runtime+Page+Faults
comments: 2026-03-13T04:10Z - Liam Chen (SRE): Performed rolling restart on runtime-tenant-045 through runtime-tenant-048. Observed KV-cache fragmentation decrease and page-faults tail off. Keeping watch for recurrence.

2026-03-13T05:22Z - Priya Shah (Customer Success): Notified NimbusAI of temporary throttle and recommended lowering concurrent streams and prefetch. Customer confirms reduced client-side concurrency during peak windows.

2026-03-13T11:04Z - Diego Ortega (Runtime Eng): Started triage on kernel_fallback logic. Initial theory: fallback activated when certain instruction set not available leading to slower memory access patterns. Created ENG-6401 to track.
2026-03-13T14:32Z - Aisha Malik (Support): Customer reports intermittent spike at 14:10Z after resuming a test burst. Re-applied temporary gateway throttle and opened coordination call for 14:45Z.
2026-03-14T09:08Z - Liam Chen (SRE): Added additional logging on routing sharding decisions for tenant pinning. Will collect 24h of data to confirm shard imbalance hypothesis.
resolution_summary: Temporary mitigations (gateway throttle, reduced prefetch, pod restarts) reduced error rate. Engineering tickets opened for kernel fallback guards, autoscaler sensitivity, gateway burst circuit-breaker, and KV-cache tuning. Working with customer on client-side limits.
next_steps: ENG to provide ETA for ENG-6401, ENG-6322, ENG-6390, ENG-6360 (targeted update by 2026-03-15)
SRE to run 24h collection of shard routing logs and present findings in postmortem
CS to coordinate a low-impact test window with NimbusAI to validate mitigations
Create postmortem doc and customer playbook entry once fixes deployed
